question.problem: Given the function $f(x,y,z)=2y{e}^{x}-{e}^{z}$, find the equation of the tangent plane to the level surface that passes through the point where $(x,y,z)=(1,1,-1).$
question.worked_solution:
The equation of the tangent plane to the level surface $f(x,y,z)=k$ at the point $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})$ can be expressed as

$$
∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩=0.
$$

First, we find the gradient of $f(x,y,z)$ and evaluate it at $({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})=(1,1,-1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇\,f(x,y,z) & ={f}_{x}(x,y,z)\,i+{f}_{y}(x,y,z)\,j+{f}_{z}(x,y,z)\,k \\  & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(2y{e}^{x}-{e}^{z})\text{ }i+\frac{∂}{∂y}(2y{e}^{x}-{e}^{z})\text{ }j+\frac{∂}{∂z}(2y{e}^{x}-{e}^{z})\text{ }k \\  & =2y{e}^{x}\text{ }i+2{e}^{x}\text{ }j-{e}^{z}k \\ ∇\,f(1,1,-1) & =2(1)e\text{ }i+2e\text{ }j-{e}^{-1}k \\  & =2e\,i+2e\,j-{e}^{-1}k \\  & =⟨2e,2e,-\frac{1}{e}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

We can now write down the Cartesian equation of the tangent plane to the level surface, as follows: 

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f({x}_{0},{y}_{0},{z}_{0})\cdot ⟨x-{x}_{0},\,y-{y}_{0},\,z-{z}_{0}⟩ & =0 \\ ∇f(1,1,-1)\cdot ⟨x-1,\,y-1,\,z+1⟩ & =0 \\ ⟨2e,2e,-\frac{1}{e}⟩\cdot ⟨x-1,\,y-1,\,z+1⟩ & =0 \\ 2ex+2ey-\frac{z}{e}-4e-\frac{1}{e} & =0\end{aligned}
$$
